record.original_question: If X is a perfect monotonically Lindelof GO-space and Y is any subspace of X, must Y itself be monotonically Lindelof, where monotonically Lindelof means that open covers admit monotone choices of countable open refinements?

evidence.quote: Question 9. If Y is a subspace of a perfect monotonically Lindelöf GO-space X, must Y be monotonically Lindelöf?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A generalized ordered space (GO-space) is a triple $(X,\tau,<)$ where $<$ is a linear order on $X$ and $\tau$ is a Hausdorff topology on $X$ having a base consisting of order-convex sets (sets $C$ such that $a,b\in C$ and $a<x<b$ imply $x\in C$). A topological space $X$ is called perfect if every closed subset of $X$ is a $G_\delta$-set.

A topological space $X$ is called monotonically Lindelöf if there is an operator $r$ assigning to every open cover $\mathcal{U}$ of $X$ a countable open refinement $r(\mathcal{U})$ of $\mathcal{U}$ that covers $X$, in such a way that whenever $\mathcal{U}$ refines $\mathcal{V}$ (i.e., every member of $\mathcal{U}$ is contained in some member of $\mathcal{V}$), the refinement $r(\mathcal{U})$ refines $r(\mathcal{V})$.

Question: Let $X$ be a perfect monotonically Lindelöf GO-space, and let $Y\subseteq X$ be an arbitrary subspace (equipped with the induced order and the subspace topology). Must $Y$ be monotonically Lindelöf?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches turned up related work (Levy–Matveev's characterization of monotonically Lindelöf GO-spaces and results showing every first-countable Lindelöf GO-space is monotonically Lindelöf), but no source explicitly resolves whether every subspace of a perfect monotonically Lindelöf GO-space must itself be monotonically Lindelöf. No published solution or counterexample to this specific hereditarity question was found.

status_evidence.title: A characterization of monotonically Lindelöf generalized ordered spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Characterization of monotonically Lindelöf GO-spaces; gives answers to questions of Levy and Matveev on monotone properties in ordered spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Related characterization work exists but does not explicitly settle the subspace question for perfect monotonically Lindelöf GO-spaces.

status_evidence.title: The monotone Lindelöf property and separability in ordered spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Studies monotone Lindelöf property in LOTS/GO-spaces and its relationship to separability.
status_evidence.claim: Background source on monotone Lindelöf in ordered spaces; does not resolve the stated hereditarity question.
